Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Right. So in the new FN rulebook, you are not allowed to Self Contest. If you
are forced to self contest, the second copy is automatically burned.

This seems very straight forward in terms of unique Master/Minion cards--you
simply can't play them. Now what does this all mean in terms of influencing out
vampires that you already control?

-Can I Govern at Superior a vampire that I already control?

-Can I do this (Govern down) if it won't bring out the vampire (say putting 3
blood on a 6 cap vampire)?

-Can I do this (Govern down) if it will (say putting 3 blood on a 2 cap
vampire)?

-Can I transfer to a vampire that I already control?

-Can I transfer enough blood to a vampire I control to bring him out?

-Am I restricted to only transfering N-1 blood to a vampire I already control,
where N is their capacity?

I am fully in favor of the No Self Contesting rule, but it strikes me that
there is an awful lot of ambiguity attatched.

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On 23 Jul 2001 20:06:13 GMT, pd...@aol.comANTISPAM (Peter D Bakija)
wrote:

>Right. So in the new FN rulebook, you are not allowed to Self Contest. If you
>are forced to self contest, the second copy is automatically burned.
>
>This seems very straight forward in terms of unique Master/Minion cards--you
>simply can't play them. Now what does this all mean in terms of influencing out
>vampires that you already control?

Standard disclaimer for others: IANALSJ. If you must be CERTAIN,
wait for him.

>-Can I Govern at Superior a vampire that I already control?

Seems logical, as long as he's younger. Governing by itself doesn't
trigger contesting.

>-Can I do this (Govern down) if it won't bring out the vampire (say putting 3
>blood on a 6 cap vampire)?

Also seems logical; still doesn't trigger contesting.

>-Can I do this (Govern down) if it will (say putting 3 blood on a 2 cap
>vampire)?

This sets up future contesting IF the vampire comes out, but the
action itself doesn't self-contest, so I'd think so. One could choose
to transfer blood -off- the vampire, for example, and avoid contesting
in that fashion.

I would also say that you were not REQUIRED to transfer blood off the
vampire once you got to your influence phase; the vampire just comes
into play and is immediately burned, per the rules.

>-Can I transfer to a vampire that I already control?

Don't see why not.

>-Can I transfer enough blood to a vampire I control to bring him out?

Since this would result in you contesting with yourself, I'd say no.

>-Am I restricted to only transfering N-1 blood to a vampire I already control,
>where N is their capacity?

This also seems logical, as the act of transferring causes an
immediate contest and there's no way for you to avoid contesting the
vampire after making the transfers.

>I am fully in favor of the No Self Contesting rule, but it strikes me that
>there is an awful lot of ambiguity attatched.

The English language is a wonderful thing. =)

-- Derek

out
>vampires that you already control?

If a second copy of a vampire you already control is moved to your
controlled
area (e.g., by being moved to your ready region at the end of your influence
phase), it is burned.

>-Can I Govern at Superior a vampire that I already control?

Yes.

>-Can I do this (Govern down) if it won't bring out the vampire (say putting 3
>blood on a 6 cap vampire)?

Yes.

>-Can I do this (Govern down) if it will (say putting 3 blood on a 2 cap
>vampire)?

Yes.

>-Can I transfer to a vampire that I already control?

Yes.

>-Can I transfer enough blood to a vampire I control to bring him out?

Yes.

>-Am I restricted to only transfering N-1 blood to a vampire I already
control,
>where N is their capacity?

No.

>I am fully in favor of the No Self Contesting rule, but it strikes me that
>there is an awful lot of ambiguity attatched.

If you like.

You cannot voluntarily play a second copy.
In the case of influenced vampires, moving the copy to your controlled area
is
not voluntary - it is mandatory when the vampire has sufficient counters on
him. [7]

If there's any ambiguity left, let me know.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Kevin wrote:
>>So there is no way I can SELF-contest Jimmy, but I can still bring out my
Jimmy
to make someone else's Jimmy go <poof!>, correct?>>

No, no, you missunderstand. It is impossible to contest anyone's Jimmy Dunn
(yours or an opponent's), by defenition. Thus, you are free to bring out a
second Jimmy Dunn, even if you already have one in play, and burn your own
first Jimmy Dunn, as he does not ever contest--he simply burns the first one.
You can bring out a Jimmy Dunn to burn your own Jimmy Dunn, or someone else's.

Jimmy Dunn completely circumvents the "you may not self contest" rule, as Jimmy
Dunn does not ever contest anyone, as per card text.
